subject: microbiology
title: Antigen-Antibody Reactions II: Western Blot, Immunofluorescence, Flow Cytometry and Rapid Tests

steps.tx: **Western blot** separates proteins by gel electrophoresis, transfers to membrane, and probes with serum so antibodies declare against individual bands (HIV gp120, gp41, p24 criteria historically), giving specificity through anatomy rather than single signals. Line immunoassays (striped antigens without electrophoresis) inherited its confirmatory role in HIV and hepatitis algorithms.
steps.say: Blot bands name the exact proteins an antibody recognises; patterns, not single lines, confirm.

steps.tx: **Immunofluorescence** lights antibody location: direct (labelled antibody finds antigen in tissue or smears, rabies and respiratory viruses) and indirect (patient antibody found by labelled anti human globulin, ANA patterns on HEp2 cells naming autoimmune targets by nuclear art). Fluorescence microscopy and fading discipline are its laboratory weather.
steps.say: Direct lights the antigen, indirect lights the patient's antibody; ANA patterns are IF art with diagnoses.

left.title: Direct IF
points: Rabies antigen in brain and skin
Skin and renal biopsy immunoglobulin deposits

right.title: Indirect IF
points: ANA patterns: homogeneous, speckled, nucleolar, centromere
ANCA patterns c and p screening

steps.tx: **Radioimmunoassay** (RIA) pioneered hormone and hepatitis measurement by radioactive competition (Yalow's Nobel), largely replaced by enzyme and chemiluminescent immunoassays for safety, its competitive logic surviving in every competitive ELISA. Competitive radioimmunoassay also measured therapeutic drugs and viral antigens when no enzyme assay existed, and its strict standard curves taught quantitative serology to a generation of laboratories before automated platforms inherited those calibration habits and quality controls.
steps.say: RIA taught competitive measurement with radioactivity; modern labels kept the logic, dropped the isotopes.

steps.tx: **Immunochromatography** (lateral flow) runs sample along a strip where labelled antigen or antibody meets capture lines (test and control), reading malaria HRP2, dengue NS1, HIV, pregnancy hCG and influenza at bedsides in minutes, trading analytical sensitivity for speed and zero infrastructure, with control line absence invalidating any result.
steps.say: No control line, no result: lateral flow's first reading rule.

left.title: Strip anatomy
points: Test line capture antigen or antibody

right.title: Rapid test traps
points: Prozone and hook at high antigen (HRP2 debates)
Heat and humidity degrade field kits
Confirmatory pathways after positives in low prevalence

steps.tx: The **prozone phenomenon** (antibody excess preventing lattice, false negative undiluted serum in agglutination and precipitation, classic in secondary syphilis RPR and brucellosis) resolves on dilution, its mirror postzone (antigen excess, hook effect in one step immunoassays at extreme hCG or prolactin) resolving likewise. Unexplained negative with strong suspicion means dilute and repeat.
steps.say: Too much antibody hides the reaction; diluting the serum reveals it.

left.title: Prozone facts
points: Antibody excess saturates sites without lattice
Laboratories reflex dilute at risk requests

right.title: Hook (postzone) facts
points: Antigen excess saturates both assay antibodies separately
Two step wash designs reduce it

steps.tx: **Flow cytometry** reappears here as an antigen antibody reaction instrument: fluorochrome conjugated monoclonal antibodies tag CD molecules (CD module), light scatter sizes cells, and thousands per second are phenotyped. Its serology sibling (bead based multiplex arrays) reads many antibodies from one sample on colour coded beads.
steps.say: Flow turns antibodies into cell counters; beads turn them into multiplex serology.

right.title: Bead arrays
points: Luminex style multiplex cytokines and antibodies

steps.tx: **Chemiluminescence immunoassays** (CLIA and electrochemiluminescence) drive modern serology automation: magnetic particle capture, light emitting labels, random access high throughput for HIV, hepatitis, TORCH and tumour markers, with grey zone and confirmatory algorithms inherited from ELISA logic at industrial scale, including reflex repeat testing, lot to lot quality control, electronic result transmission and delta checks that flag implausible changes between a patient current and previous specimen.
steps.say: Chemiluminescence is ELISA with light and robots; algorithms still outrank single values.

left.title: Platform facts
points: Wide dynamic ranges, low detection limits
STAT random access for emergency serology

right.title: Interpretation discipline
points: Signal to cut off ratios guide confirms
Repeat in duplicate for critical positives by policy

steps.tx: **Assay interference literacy** closes serology: rheumatoid factor bridges IgM assays falsely, heterophile and human anti mouse antibodies bridge sandwiches, high dose biotin (supplements) breaks streptavidin capture, haemolysis, lipaemia and icterus disturb photometry, each with a dilution, blocking or alternate platform answer. A result that contradicts the patient is an assay first.
steps.say: When serology contradicts the patient, interrogate the assay before the diagnosis.
